title: How to Create and Customize Your Profile on ConnectPi Web
summary: Complete guide to updating your display name, bio, avatar, and social links on ConnectPi.
body: Your ConnectPi profile is your decentralized identity across the Pioneer social ecosystem. Customizing your profile helps you connect with fellow Pioneers, gain followers, and showcase your community contributions. Step by Step Profile Customization Follow these steps to update your personal information and profile appearance: Open your browser and visit: connectpi.in/profile Alternatively, you can click on Profile under the MY SPACE section in the left navigation sidebar. On your main profile overview, locate the Edit Profile button positioned directly below your cover banner, adjacent to your username handle. The Edit Profile modal will open with the following fields: Avatar Photo: Click the camera icon overlaid on your profile picture to upload a new avatar (JPG, PNG, or WebP). Name \ : Enter your preferred display name. This is the name shown in bold across all your posts, replies, and community feeds. Email: Provide your contact email address (kept private and used for account notifications). Bio: Write a brief introduction about yourself, your Pioneer journey, or your community interests. Links (comma separated): Add external websites, social profiles, or community channels (separate multiple URLs with commas). Once you have updated your information, click the blue Save Changes button in the bottom right corner of the dialog. Your profile will refresh and update immediately! Custom username modification is currently not available on the Web platform. Your username (handle) is permanently linked to your verified registration identifier (such as your Pi Network UID or auto assigned Google handle). A dedicated feature allowing Pioneers to customize or upgrade their username (through future free or premium plan updates) is currently under development. Exploring Profile Features Your ConnectPi profile includes several tools to manage your presence and rewards: View Card: Explore your personalized Profile Card —a shareable digital badge with custom links, QR code, and subscription options. Analytics: Track impressions, post reach, follower growth, and community engagement metrics. Claim Pi & Loyalty Points: Access your daily check in rewards and view your loyalty points balance. Posts & Bookmarks Tabs: Easily filter between your published community posts and articles you have bookmarked for later reading. ConnectPi adheres to strict privacy principles. Your sensitive account details—including your private Pi wallet keys and internal credentials—are never exposed publicly on your profile page.

title: How to Create and Publish Posts on ConnectPi Web
summary: Comprehensive guide to publishing posts, attaching media, clipboard pasting, character limits, and audience visibility on ConnectPi.
headings: 2. Composing Your Post & Using Media Tools
body: ConnectPi is the social home for the global Pi Network community. Creating posts lets you share updates, trade ideas, discuss Pioneer initiatives, and earn engagement rewards. 1. Opening the Post Creator You can start creating a post from several convenient locations across the platform: On Desktop & Laptops When browsing connectpi.in on your computer, you have two instant entry points: Option A (Sidebar): Click the purple + New Post button in the left navigation sidebar. Option B (Home Banner): Click the white Create Post button (or the "What's happening in Pi Network...?" prompt) in the central home feed banner. On Mobile Devices & Pi Browser When accessing ConnectPi on your mobile phone: Option A (Home Banner): Tap the Create Post button in the top banner. Option B (Floating Action Button): Tap the round blue (+) Floating Action Button (FAB) fixed at the bottom right corner of your screen. 2. Composing Your Post & Using Media Tools Clicking any of the post buttons opens the Create a new post modal editor: Type your message into the "What's happening...?" text area. Standard Accounts: Up to 350 characters . Premium Accounts: Up to 700 characters with a verified blue Pioneer badge. A live character counter in the bottom right corner displays your remaining allowance. You can enrich your post with media through three flexible methods: File Picker: Click the Gallery (Image) icon or Camera (Video) icon in the bottom toolbar to upload media files from your device. Drag & Drop: Drag an image or video directly from your computer files and drop it onto the dialog. Clipboard Paste: Copy any screenshot ( Ctrl+C or Cmd+C ) and press Ctrl+V inside the editor to upload instantly! Click the @ icon (or type @ in your text) to search for any registered Pioneer by username and tag them with instant autocomplete. Use hashtags (e.g. PiNetwork , ConnectPi , Crypto ) to group your post with trending discussions. Under "Who can see this post?" , select your target distribution: ALL: Broadcasted across all public feeds. Global: Featured in international discovery feeds. Local: Targeted to Pioneers in your geographic region (requires enabling Share Location ). Click Choose under the category selector to tag your post (e.g. General , Pi Network , Tech , Marketplace , or Governance ). Categorizing posts helps other Pioneers discover your content. Review your post and tap the blue Post button in the bottom right corner. Your content is published live immediately! Once you click Post , your content is published to the public ConnectPi decentralized social network. Any Pioneer worldwide can view your post, interact with comments, or download public media attachments. Please ensure your content adheres to ConnectPi Community Guidelines . Never share personal financial keys, passwords, or confidential private data in public posts. 3. Post Limits Comparison | Feature | Standard Account | ConnectPi Premium | | |: :|: :| | Character Limit | 350 characters | 700 characters | | Media Attachments per Post | 1 file | Up to 5 files | | Daily Media Posts | 3 posts | 5 posts | | Verified Blue Badge | — | Included (Note: Golden badges are strictly reserved for official ConnectPi admins) | | Ad Free Browsing | — | Included |

title: How to Sign In to ConnectPi with Pi Network
summary: Step-by-step guide to signing in to ConnectPi Web inside the Pi Browser or external browsers.
headings: Method 1: Inside Pi Browser (Recommended for Mobile)
Method 2: Outside Pi Browser (Desktop, Chrome, or Any Standard Browser)
Can I change my display name after signing in?
body: ConnectPi utilizes official Pi Network Authentication so Pioneers can seamlessly create an account and sign in without remembering separate passwords. Your account is securely linked to your verified Pi identity. There are two primary methods to sign in depending on whether you are using the mobile Pi Browser or an external browser. Method 1: Inside Pi Browser (Recommended for Mobile) Signing in through the official Pi Browser provides instant, one tap authentication verified directly by the Pi ecosystem. Launch the official Pi Browser on your smartphone. In the URL address bar at the top of the Pi Browser, enter either of the following addresses: https://connectpi.in/signup https://aditya.pinet.com/signup On the Join or Login to Connect Pi welcome screen, locate the PI BROWSER section at the top and tap the blue Continue with Pi button. An official Pi Network dialog titled 'Share information with Connect Pi ?' will appear. ConnectPi requests the following standard permissions: Auth: Authenticates you on ConnectPi with your verified Pi identity. Username: Synchronizes your public Pi username. Wallet address: Connects your public wallet address for community tipping and reward distributions. In app notifications: Allows the app to notify you about likes, comments, and community updates. Tap the purple Allow button to confirm. Your account is instantly verified and created (or logged in). You will be redirected straight to your ConnectPi community feed where you can start engaging with fellow Pioneers. Official Pi authentication occurs entirely through the automated Pi SDK dialog shown above. ConnectPi will NEVER ask you to enter, paste, or share your 24 word Pi wallet passphrase . If any website asks for your passphrase, close it immediately. Method 2: Outside Pi Browser (Desktop, Chrome, or Any Standard Browser) If you are accessing ConnectPi from a laptop, desktop computer, or any standard mobile browser (such as Google Chrome, Apple Safari, Microsoft Edge, Brave, or Firefox), you can securely log in using a Pi QR Code linked to your phone's Pi Browser. Open your web browser and go to: connectpi.in/signup Scroll to the DESKTOP / CHROME / ANY BROWSER card and click the Sign in with Pi Account button. You will be securely redirected to the official Pi Network authentication portal on accounts.pinet.com . A unique Sign in with Pi QR code will appear on your screen. 1. Open your phone's standard Camera app (or any QR scanner app). 2. Point your camera at the QR code displayed on your desktop monitor. 3. Tap the link banner or pop up notification that appears on your phone screen. The scanned link automatically opens the Pi Browser app on your phone, displaying the 'Share information with Connect Pi ?' authorization screen. Tap the purple Allow button. Once you tap Allow on your phone, your desktop browser will automatically detect the authorization in real time. It will instantly log in or register your account and redirect you directly to your ConnectPi community feed! With QR code authentication, you never have to type passwords or passphrases on your desktop. Your session is securely authenticated through your phone's trusted Pi Browser. Frequently Asked Questions Can I change my display name after signing in? Yes. Your Pi username is permanently attached as your unique Pioneer identifier, but you can set and update your custom profile display name, bio, and avatar anytime under Profile Settings . What happens if I click 'Decline'? If you select Decline on the Pi permissions modal, ConnectPi cannot verify your Pi account, and you will not be able to log in. You can simply tap Continue with Pi again and choose Allow whenever you are ready.

title: How to Sign Up and Login with Google on ConnectPi Web
summary: Step-by-step guide to creating your ConnectPi account using Google authentication and logging in with credentials.
headings: Part 1: How to Sign Up with Google
Part 2: How to Log In with Your Credentials
body: In addition to Pi Network authentication, ConnectPi Web allows Pioneers to create an account using Google Authentication and log in securely with their email/username and password. Part 1: How to Sign Up with Google Follow these steps to register your ConnectPi account using your Google profile: Open your browser and navigate to: connectpi.in/signup google Before proceeding, you must check both required confirmation boxes: 1. Terms & Policies: Agree to ConnectPi's Terms of Service , Privacy Policy , and Refund Policy . 2. Age of Majority: Confirm that you have reached the legal age of majority in your jurisdiction (at least 18 years old). Both checkboxes must be selected for the authentication button to activate. Click the blue Authenticate with Google button and choose your preferred Google account from the standard Google Sign In prompt. Once authenticated, ConnectPi verifies your email address as your unique identifier and provides an auto generated username. Click the Continue button. You will be prompted to enter: Display Name: Your community name visible on posts and comments. Bio: A brief introduction about yourself. Avatar: An optional profile picture. Password: Choose a secure password for your account. Submit the form to finalize your account registration! On the Web version, Google sign up assigns an auto generated username. If you want to select a custom username during registration, download the official ConnectPi Mobile App for Android: 👉 Download ConnectPi on Google Play Store (Package ID: in.connectpi.app ) Part 2: How to Log In with Your Credentials Once your account has been registered, you can log in directly at any time using your username/email and password: Go to: connectpi.in/login In the Username or UID field, type your registered username, email address, or UID. In the Password field, type your account password. Click the blue Login button. You will be authenticated immediately and taken to your personal ConnectPi home feed.

title: Troubleshooting Pi Browser Login and Authentication Timeouts
summary: Step-by-step resolution for Pi SDK loading errors, 60-second timeouts, WebView cache conflicts, and authentication failures.
body: If you experience an infinite loading spinner, an authentication timeout, or an error when logging into ConnectPi via Pi Browser, follow this comprehensive troubleshooting guide. 1. Common Symptoms & Root Causes | Error / Symptom | Primary Cause | Quick Fix | | | | | | "Pi SDK not loaded. Please use the Pi Browser." | Opened in Chrome, Safari, or an external browser instead of Pi Browser. | Open connectpi.in inside Pi Browser, or use the Desktop QR flow. | | Connecting spinner hangs 60 seconds | Pi Browser WebView session cache is desynchronized or unresponsive. | Force close Pi Browser and clear temporary cache. | | "Authentication verification failed" | Pi Network core API ( api.minepi.com ) timeout or expired session token. | Tap Try Again to request a fresh authentication grant. | | "Authentication was cancelled" | The permission prompt was dismissed or Decline was tapped. | Click Continue with Pi again and tap Allow . | | Incomplete Payment dialog appears | A previous Pi transaction was interrupted before server settlement. | Wait 5 seconds while ConnectPi auto resolves pending transactions. | 2. Step by Step Resolution Procedures Ensure you are using the official Pi Browser application: 1. Open the Pi Browser app on your mobile device. 2. Enter https://connectpi.in/signup or https://aditya.pinet.com/signup in the top address bar. 3. Ensure the protocol is https:// to allow secure WebView cryptographic bridges. Corrupted WebView cache is the most frequent cause of frozen authentication dialogs. On Android: 1. Open your phone's Settings Apps (or Manage Apps ). 2. Locate and tap Pi Browser . 3. Tap Force Stop . 4. Go to Storage & Cache tap Clear Cache ( do not select Clear Data/Storage ). 5. Reopen Pi Browser and navigate back to connectpi.in . On iOS (iPhone): 1. Swipe up from the bottom of your screen to open the app switcher. 2. Swipe up on Pi Browser to force close it. 3. Turn your phone's Airplane Mode ON for 5 seconds, then turn it back OFF to reset network sockets. 4. Reopen Pi Browser. The Pi Browser relies on the background session from your primary Pi Network app: 1. Open the official Pi Network mining app on your phone. 2. Ensure your account is actively logged in and your mining session is current. 3. Tap the side menu in the Pi app tap Pi Browser select Sign in to Pi Browser . This refreshes the underlying cryptographic bridge between both apps. When the Share information with ConnectPi? sheet appears, verify the requested scopes: Auth: Authenticate you with your Pi account. Username: Your verified Pi handle. Wallet address: Your public wallet address for social tipping and marketplace transactions. In app notifications: Platform alerts and message updates. Tap the purple Allow button. If you tap Decline , authentication cannot proceed. If the mobile Pi Browser WebView is experiencing persistent issues: 1. Open https://connectpi.in/signup on your computer or secondary device. 2. Select Sign in with Pi Account under Desktop / Chrome / Any Browser . 3. Scan the generated QR code using your phone's camera to authorize securely via accounts.pinet.com . Never enter or share your 24 word Pi Passphrase! ConnectPi uses official Pi Network SDK OAuth protocols. Legitimate authentication never asks for your passphrase, private keys, or wallet seed phrase. Anyone asking for your 24 words is an unauthorized imposter attempting to steal your funds. 3. Still Unable to Log In? If you have completed all troubleshooting steps and still cannot authenticate: Check the official Pi Core Team status channels for network wide API maintenance. If your account registered via Google, you can log in directly at https://connectpi.in/login with your username or email and password. Reach out to our Pioneer support team with your registered Pi username and device model.

title: Installing the ConnectPi Android App from Google Play Store
summary: Step-by-step guide to installing the official ConnectPi Android app, choosing custom usernames, configuring permissions, and connecting your Pi account.
body: The native ConnectPi Android App delivers the fastest mobile social experience for Pioneers worldwide, featuring real time push notifications, offline feed caching, daily reward streak reminders, and custom username creation. 1. Why Download the Android App? While ConnectPi Web is accessible from any desktop or mobile browser, the native Android app unlocks exclusive mobile benefits: Custom Username Selection: Choose your own unique Pioneer handle (e.g. @pioneer alex ) during registration, rather than receiving an auto generated username. Instant Push Alerts: Get real time notifications when Pioneers mention you, comment on your posts, or send peer messages. Daily Check in & Quests: Never miss your daily CP token claim with streak reminder notifications. Integrated Camera & Media: Snap photos and record videos directly inside the post editor without leaving the application. 2. Installation via Google Play Store Follow these steps to install the official app safely on your Android device: Open the official ConnectPi store page on your Android smartphone: 👉 Download Connect Pi on Google Play Store (Package ID: in.connectpi.app | Verified Developer: Connect Pi) Tap the green Install button. The Play Store will verify the package signature and download the application ( 30–45 MB). Once installation finishes, tap Open or launch the Connect Pi app icon from your home screen or app drawer. 3. Account Setup & Custom Username Selection When you launch ConnectPi for the first time, you can sign in with your existing account or create a brand new Pioneer profile: Choose Sign up with Google or Continue with Pi Network . Unlike the web onboarding flow which assigns an automatic handle, the Android app provides an interactive Username Picker : Choose a unique handle (e.g. yourname or pioneer crypto ). Usernames can contain lowercase alphanumeric letters, digits, and underscores. ConnectPi will check availability in real time. Add your display name, a brief bio introducing yourself to the community, and upload a profile avatar. 4. App Permissions Guide To deliver core community features, ConnectPi requests standard Android runtime permissions. Here is why each permission is required: | Permission | Category | Purpose in ConnectPi | Mandatory? | | | | |: :| | POST NOTIFICATIONS | Notifications | Delivers instant alerts for daily CP check in rewards, mentions, and incoming direct messages. | Recommended | | CAMERA | Media Capture | Allows taking live photos and short videos directly within the post composer. | Optional | | READ MEDIA IMAGES | Storage / Gallery | Required to select and upload photos or screenshots from your photo gallery. | Recommended | | ACCESS COARSE LOCATION | Location | Powers the optional Locality Feed and regional Pioneer marketplace discovery. | Optional | You can manage or revoke optional permissions (such as Location or Camera) at any time from your device's Settings Apps Connect Pi Permissions . 5. System Requirements & Specifications Operating System: Android 8.0 (API Level 26) or higher (Android 9.0+ recommended). Free Storage Space: Minimum 50 MB for app installation and media cache. Internet Connectivity: Stable 4G, 5G, or Wi Fi connection. Package Identifier: in.connectpi.app Always verify that you are downloading ConnectPi with the exact package ID in.connectpi.app on the official Google Play Store. Never install APK files from untrusted third party websites or Telegram groups. Remember: ConnectPi will never ask for your 24 word Pi wallet passphrase.

title: How to report a bug or submit feedback
summary: Help improve ConnectPi by sending diagnostic info, screenshots, and reproduction steps.
headings: What to include in a bug report
body: Found a glitch or an unexpected behavior? Reporting clear steps helps our engineering team deploy rapid bug fixes. What to include in a bug report 1. Device & OS: What phone or browser (e.g. Android 13, Pi Browser v1.6.1, Chrome 122). 2. Steps to reproduce: What action you performed immediately prior to the error. 3. Expected vs Actual behavior: What should have happened compared to what actually happened. Use our structured contact form to automatically attach device and browser diagnostics.
